title: My day
goal: Describe your daily routine from getting up to going to bed, and use adverbs of frequency — twenty new verbs that all use the six endings from unit 4.
bekal: describe your daily routine from morning to night

dialogs.title: خبرې اترې — سهار په کور کې
dialogs.intro: Early morning in the kitchen. Zarghuna has finished the dawn prayer and is making tea when Budi comes downstairs.

lines.speaker: زرغونه:
lines.text: سهار مو پخیر! تاسو ژر پاڅېدلئ.
lines.baca: sahār mo pəkhayr! tāso zhər pātsedəy.
lines.id: Good morning! You're up very early.
lines.literal: morning your(pl) with-goodness! you(pl) early get-up-you(pl).

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: سهار مو پخیر. زه تل ژر پاڅېږم.
lines.baca: sahār mo pəkhayr. zə təl zhər pātsīẓəm.
lines.id: Good morning. I always get up early.
lines.literal: morning your(pl) with-goodness. I always early get-up-I.

lines.speaker: زرغونه:
lines.text: زه هم. لومړی لمونځ کوم، بیا چای جوړوم.
lines.baca: zə ham. lūmṛay lmūndz kawəm, byā chāy joṛawəm.
lines.id: Me too. First I pray, then I make tea.
lines.literal: I also. first prayer do-I, then tea make-I.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.id: What do you eat every day?

lines.speaker: زرغونه:
lines.text: سهار ډوډۍ او چای. غرمه وریجې. ماښام غوښه او ډوډۍ.
lines.baca: sahār ḍoḍəy aw chāy. gharma wrīje. māṣām ghwaṣa aw ḍoḍəy.
lines.id: Bread and tea in the morning. Rice at midday. Meat and bread in the evening.
lines.literal: morning bread and tea. midday rice. evening meat and bread.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.id: And what do you do after that?

lines.speaker: زرغونه:
lines.text: زه ښوونځي ته ځم. زه ښوونکې یم.
lines.baca: zə ṣowundzī ta dzəm. zə ṣowunke yəm.
lines.id: I go to school. I'm a teacher.
lines.literal: I school to go-I. I teacher(f) am-I.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.id: How many hours do you work?

lines.speaker: زرغونه:
lines.text: شپږ ساعته. ماسپښین کور ته راځم او آرام کوم.
lines.baca: shpaẓ sā'ata. māspaṣīn kor ta rādzəm aw ārām kawəm.
lines.id: Six hours. In the afternoon I come home and rest.
lines.literal: six hours. afternoon home to come-I and rest do-I.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.id: Do you sometimes go to the market?

lines.speaker: زرغونه:
lines.text: هو، خو هېڅکله یوازې نه ځم. تل زما مور راسره وي.
lines.baca: ho, kho hetskəla yawāze nə dzəm. təl zmā mor rāsara wī.
lines.id: Yes, but I never go alone. My mother always comes with me.
lines.literal: yes, but never alone not go-I. always of-me mother with-me usually-is.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.id: What do you do in the evening?

lines.speaker: زرغونه:
lines.text: کتاب لولم یا د کورنۍ سره خبرې کوم. بالاخره لس بجې ویده کېږم.
lines.baca: kitāb lwaləm yā də kornəy sara khabare kawəm. bilākhira las baje wīdə keẓəm.
lines.id: I read books or chat with the family. Finally, at ten, I go to sleep.
lines.literal: book read-I or of family with talk do-I. finally ten o'clock asleep become-I.

lines.speaker: زرغونه:
lines.text: دلته هره ورځ سره ورته وي. خو جمعه بېله ده!
lines.baca: dəlta hara wradz sara warta wī. kho juma bela da!
lines.id: Here every day is much the same. But Friday is different!
lines.literal: here every day together alike usually-is. but Friday different is!

notes: Notice that every verb in this dialogue uses the same six endings from unit 4: پاڅېږم، کوم، خورم، ځم، راځم، لولم، کېږم. No helper verbs, no separate "-ing" form — the Pashto present means both "I am doing" and "I usually do".
The verb جوړول means "to make" in the sense of putting together or fixing: چای جوړوم (I make tea), کور جوړوم (I build a house). It is different from کول, which means to do an action.
The phrase لمونځ کول means to pray, literally "to do prayer". This pattern of noun plus کول forms hundreds of Pashto verbs — you have already seen it in کار کول (to work) and خبرې کول (to talk).

The word راسره means "with me", and it combines را (direction toward me) and سره (with). Similar forms: ورسره (with him/her), درسره (with you). These little words را، ور، در are direction markers, and they come back in unit 17.

Notice the verb وي *wī* in the last line, which differs from دي. The form دي means "is/are right now", while وي means "usually is" or "tends to be". The sentence هره ورځ سره ورته **وي** means "every day is usually alike", not "today is alike".

The sequence words for telling a story — لومړی (first), بیا (then), وروسته (after that), بالاخره (finally) — will make your story sound organized even while your vocabulary is still small. These four words are worth more than twenty new nouns.

grammars.title: Adverbs of frequency, and where they go
body: Pashto puts frequency words **before the verb**, usually right after the subject. The order: subject, frequency word, object, verb. For example زه **تل** ژر پاڅېږم.

⚠️ The word هېڅکله (never) still needs نه in front of the verb. The sentence is زه هېڅکله یوازې **نه** ځم, with two negative markers at once — something standard English forbids ("I never don't go") but Pashto requires.

grammars.title: Two words for "is" with different jobs: دي and وي
body: The forms دی، ده، دي state how things are **now, at this moment**: هوا نن سړه ده (the weather is cold today). The form وي states how things **usually are**: هوا په ژمي کې سړه وي (the weather is usually cold in winter).

English marks this difference only with words like "usually", and beginners almost always use دی for both. You will still be understood, but using وي correctly is one of the quickest signs that you are no longer a beginner.

sections.title: Twenty verbs for a whole day

blocks.text: Telling a story: four words that put everything in order

blocks.title: Tea, and why it is more than a drink
items: There are two kinds you need to be able to name: **شین چای** *shīn chāy* (green tea, most common in the south and west) and **تور چای** *tor chāy* (black tea, more common in the east and north).
Offering tea is not small talk; refusing it outright can come across as cold. If you really don't want any, accept the cup and take a small sip — that is enough.
Phrases you will hear: **چای وڅښئ** *chāy wətsṣəy* (please have some tea) and **یو پیاله نوره** *yaw pyāla nora* (one more cup). A polite way to decline: **بس دی، مننه** *bas day, manana*.
⚠️ Sugar is served separately and often held in the mouth, not stirred in. If you want sweet tea, ask for **خوږ چای** *khwaẓ chāy*.

blocks.title: Telling your day in five sentences
items: Always start with when you get up: زه شپږ بجې پاڅېږم.
Go on with breakfast: بیا ډوډۍ خورم او چای څښم.
Mention work or study: زه اته بجې کار ته ځم.
Mention the afternoon: ماسپښین کور ته راځم او آرام کوم.
Close with bedtime: بالاخره لس بجې ویده کېږم.
These five sentences are a frame you can refill for life. Change one verb every day and you will have twenty different stories in a month.
I always get up at six.
First I pray, then I drink tea.
I work six hours.
Sometimes I go to the market.
Finally I go to sleep at ten.
